name: Lynx Punchout
author: lynxmarket

sections.description:
Large customers often buy through a procurement system (SAP SRM, SAP Ariba, Coupa and others). They expect suppliers to offer a punchout catalogue: the buyer opens your shop from their procurement system, fills a cart, and the cart goes back to the procurement system instead of going through your checkout.

Try it as a buyer, without any procurement system: live demo.

Lynx Punchout adds this to a WooCommerce shop:

  • SAP OCI and cXML punchout, from the same shop.
  • The buyer is logged in automatically with the customer account you choose, so they see their own prices and catalogue.
  • On the cart page, the checkout button is replaced by “Transfer to your procurement system” for punchout sessions only. Your regular customers are not affected.
  • cXML edit and inspect operations are supported (the previous cart is reloaded; inspect is read-only).
  • Buyers are managed from your WordPress admin: login, password, allowed return domains, linked customer account.
  • Compatible with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage. The plugin never creates or changes orders.

This plugin needs the Lynx Punchout service

The plugin is the WordPress side of a hosted service. The Lynx Punchout gateway receives the punchout requests of the procurement systems, checks the buyer’s credentials, and converts the cart to the OCI or cXML format expected by each system. The plugin cannot do punchout without it.

The service is paid: 9 EUR per month or 90 EUR per year, per shop, after a 14-day free trial that needs no payment details. All the code of the plugin is included and nothing in it is locked; without an active subscription the service stops accepting punchout sessions and cart transfers.

External services

This plugin connects to the Lynx Punchout gateway (https://api.lynx-market.cloud), operated by Lynx Market. Nothing is sent before you click “Activate” on the plugin’s settings page.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you click “Activate”: your site address, your site name and a single-use verification code. The gateway then calls your site back once to deliver the shop ID and licence key.
  • When you manage buyers: the buyer’s login, password (stored hashed by the gateway), allowed return domains and the login of the linked WordPress account.
  • When a buyer opens a punchout session: the single-use token received in the link, to obtain the session details.
  • When a buyer transfers a cart: the cart lines (product ID, SKU, name, quantity, price excluding tax, currency) and the site language. No customer address or payment data is sent.
  • When you click “Test connection”: a signed empty request.

Requests are signed with your licence key and sent over HTTPS.

The subscription is paid with PayPal on PayPal’s own pages; the plugin only links to them.

  • Service terms: https://lynx-market.cloud/conditions/
  • Privacy policy: https://lynx-market.cloud/confidentialite/
  • PayPal privacy statement: https://www.paypal.com/webapps/mpp/ua/privacy-full
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. Go to WooCommerce > Lynx Punchout and click “Activate”. This creates your shop on the gateway and starts the free trial.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Punchout buyers and add a buyer: the login and password your customer will enter in their procurement system, the domain of that system, and the WordPress customer account the buyer will shop with.
  4. Give your customer the OCI or cXML address shown at the top of the buyers page, with the login and password.
  5. Ask your customer to open the catalogue from their procurement system and transfer a test cart.
sections.faq:
Does it change the shop for my regular customers?

No. The transfer button and the checkout redirection apply only during a punchout session.

Which accounts can a buyer be linked to?

Customer accounts only. Administrators, shop managers and other staff accounts are refused, so a punchout link can never open a privileged session.

Why must the REST API be reachable for activation?

The gateway delivers your licence key to your site itself, to prove that the site address is yours. If a security plugin blocks the REST API for visitors, allow the route lynx-punchout/v1/activate or enter the shop ID and licence key by hand.

What happens when the subscription ends?

Punchout sessions and cart transfers stop. Your shop keeps working normally for everyone else. Uninstalling the plugin removes its settings and user flags.

My procurement system needs a specific field or unit.

Contact us: field mappings are handled on the gateway, without changing the plugin.
sections.changelog:
0.3.6

  • Default UNSPSC code for cXML carts (setting), used when a product and its categories have none.
  • Works when the procurement system shows the shop in a frame: during a punchout session on HTTPS, login and cart cookies are sent with SameSite=None and Partitioned.
  • French translation: typographic spaces.

0.3.5

  • Hardening: only administrators can change the gateway address.

0.3.4

  • Declares the WooCommerce dependency (Requires Plugins).
  • Shop managers can save the settings.
  • Hardening: activation endpoint checks the challenge in its permission callback; return form escaped at output, no inline event handlers; unknown charsets fall back to UTF-8.

0.3.3

  • Works with the block-based Cart (default in recent WooCommerce): during a punchout session the cart shows the transfer button.
  • Activation message no longer announces a free trial when none is available.

0.3.2

  • During a punchout session, orders can no longer be placed through the WooCommerce Store API or the classic checkout endpoint; the read-only cart (cXML inspect) is also enforced there.

0.3.1

  • Prices shown without tax wording.

0.3.0

  • Self-service activation and buyer management from the WordPress admin.

0.2.1

  • Yearly subscription.

0.2.0

  • PayPal subscription links.

0.1.0

  • First version: OCI and cXML punchout, cart transfer.
